caption: The drawing shows a detailed side view of a four-wheeled carriage with large, thin, spoked wheels; the two front wheels are slightly smaller than the rear wheels. The carriage body is painted primarily in shades of cream, with red and dark lines as trim details along its contours. An arched, canvas or fabric canopy, tinted beige and attached with dark brown supports, covers the seating area, providing overhead shelter. The seat inside is colored light blue, with some cushion texture visible. The carriage features long, curved handles extending backward, ending in wood-toned grips. Small metallic elements, like bolts and axle hardware, are visible on the wheel hubs and along the canopy supports. In the upper right corner of the drawing, there is a small, line-art diagram of the carriage with dimensions labeled, showing the general shape and size (58 inches long and 42 inches tall). The artist’s signature and the year (Vincent P. Rasel, Del. 1864) along with "Gordon Salata" are written in the bottom right corner of the drawing. The entire drawing is set inside a thin, rectangular border on a cream-colored background.
title: Baby Carriage
